reference.
Nevertheless, it is not clear for me from the User's Guide how I have
to specify this reference in the GladModel.
In the example bellow, I consider 4 arrays. The "Bf" and "T" arrays
corresponding to blood tissues and Tumor tissues, respectively.
I would like to estimate the CNs of the "T" relative to the "Bf".

Dear Henrik,

Since almost everything works fine, I give you only a brief report of

Then, I perform the RmaCnPlm fit which gives at least 50 warnings (all
the same):
NaNs produced in: log(y, base = 2)

In the code related to the fragment length normalization (from your
example page),

cesFlnList <- list();
for (chipType in names(csList)) {
ces <- cesCnList[[chipType]];
fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(ces);
print(fln);
cesFln <- process(fln, verbose=verbose);
cesFlnList[[chipType]] <- cesFln;
}

the object "csList" and "cesCnList" are not previously defined.
Then, I substituted both names in the code by the name "cesList".
Is it correct?

The normalization seems to work fine and gives only the warning
(twice):
In getData.SnpInformation(this, ..., fields = "fragmentLength") :
NAs introducidos por coerción

The CbsModel requires the DNAcopy package, I installed from the
bioconductor repository.
The version of this package I got is the 1.11.2.
I got no error in this process.

Finally, the generation of the ChromosomeExplorer report give no error
and I obtain the images for both tumor cases for different scales.
Nevertheless, when I open the file ChromosomeExplorer.html with
Firefox, the explorer does not find these images.
Note, that in my experience this is the first time the
ChromosomeExplorer does not work.

Best regards. Olivier

The HTML page of the explorer loads Javascripts in ../../includes/
(among others). Since the HTML/Javascript pages have been updated you
might experience problems with different versions not being
compatible. In this latest version I tried to modify the HTML page to
make use of a new set of Javascripts with different names to avoid
conflicts with previous. You might want to delete all
reports/includes/js/ChromosomeExplorer*/ directories. This will force
process() to install the new ones. Let us know if it works.

parts: Hi.

On 10/2/07, Olivier <nu...@est-econ.uc3m.es> wrote:
>

> Hi,
>
> I eventually solve roughly the problem I got with
> ChromosomeExplorer.html by substituting it by a similar file :
> a ChromosomeExplorer.html file generated by an older version of
> aroma.affymetrix.
>
> About the regions.xls (a list of annotated breakpoints, I guess) the
> column call is now missing!

That could be because I know harmonized code for GLAD and CBS, and
forgot about the GLAD specific column(s).

However, unless you fine tune the GLAD parameters I would not rely
fully on the GLAD 'call':s. It also depends on what kind of data you
have. See their paper for more details.

> Moreover, in an older version of this file obtained by fitting the
> gladModel using the robust average of the samples as a reference set,
> I get the following list of breakpoints for chormosome 1, 21 and 22
> from one particular sample:
>
> sample chromosome start stop mean count call
> Bf14203 1 792429 77218238 -0.01 13032 neutral
> Bf14203 1 77219051 77244574 -0.551 5 neutral
> Bf14203 1 77256764 211216828 -0.003 20466 neutral
> Bf14203 1 211218311 211225731 -0.668 2 neutral
> Bf14203 1 211227570 245378187 -0.007 6715 neutral
> Bf14203 21 9887804 46902240 -0.002 7125 neutral
> Bf14203 22 14433758 17005919 0.087 341 gain
> Bf14203 22 17006930 19784562 -0.056 339 neutral
> Bf14203 22 19785571 49519949 0.133 5527 gain
>
> Actually, I am not sure that it is a list of breakpoints since the
> sequence of calls on the first chromosome contain the same state:
> neutral. How can I interpret this list of calls?

See paper. I believe this is because they call the regions using
pruning an hierarchical clustering trying to find global cut offs from
the data in order to get three states, loss, neutral, and gain.
Again, this is a bit ad hoc and success depends very much on what kind
of data you have and noise levels etc. I would not trust it.

I treat the the list of identified regions as a first rough guide. I
prefer to get false positives rather than miss true positive. The way
we have worked is that we often filter regions out "manually" to get a
smaller list that is later validated by other means.

Cheers

Henrik
